blacklistabilityReview.evidence: HOLLAR is Possible, not direct Yes. Census fetched 2026-10-19 puts 100% of tracked supply on Hydration (12,922,652 HOLLAR). At Hydration EVM block 15966310, hasRole(DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, 0xaa7e0000000000000000000000000000000aa7e0)=true and delegatedToken()=0x0000000000000000000000000000000100000000. The pinned GhoToken source (commit 7bbf3e1dc03313db72c1ad488aaa56c55b6e299c, src/contracts/gho/GhoToken.sol) gates setDelegatedToken(address) behind DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE; src/contracts/gho/ERC20.sol transferFrom consults delegatedToken.allowance(from, msg.sender) only for the caller and only when that allowance exceeds the amount. The currently configured precompile therefore provides no arbitrary-holder transfer. Arbitrary seizure requires the admin/OpenGov to retarget delegatedToken to an allowance-returning contract, or to replace runtime logic through the OpenGov root track. That is an admin/DAO-upgradable control surface: Possible. The current implementation has no direct blacklist, per-account freeze, or forced-transfer entry point. Hydration OpenGov root track retains runtime-upgrade authority.

oracleRisk.summary: HOLLAR uses Hydration's enshrined per-block money-market oracles and automated partial-liquidation engine across its governance-enabled collateral set; public protocol docs do not identify a secondary oracle or a separate bad-debt backstop.

branchApplicability.rationale: HOLLAR can be minted against multiple reserves with asset-specific LTV and liquidation parameters. Hydration documents one common Borrow engine, per-block oracle update path, and automated liquidation mechanism, so those reserves are represented as one grouped collateral branch without inventing reserve-level thresholds.

branches.fallbackBehavior: Hydration documents oracle updates at the beginning of every block but does not identify a secondary price source or a failover mode for unavailable or invalid reserve prices.

collateralParameters.asset: Governance-enabled Hydration Borrow collateral reserves for HOLLAR
collateralParameters.note: Each reserve has its own displayed LTV and liquidation threshold; HOLLAR positions are exposed to liquidation once their aggregate health factor falls below 1.0. No static per-reserve values are asserted here.

branches.liquidationMechanism: Hydration evaluates positions at the beginning of each block and automatically performs partial liquidations to restore health. Its Borrow overview also documents protocol custom flash loans that repay debt, swap seized collateral through the Omnipool, and burn the flash-minted amount.
branches.backstop: The documented liquidation path uses protocol-funded custom flash loans and Omnipool execution rather than requiring liquidator capital; the reviewed docs do not identify a separate reserve or insurance backstop for residual debt.
branches.shutdownOrBadDebtBehavior: Hydration's public HOLLAR and Borrow documentation does not specify an oracle-failure shutdown state or how debt remaining after failed liquidation execution is allocated, so no stronger recovery claim is made.
